title: Halwa Puri Breakfast

description: Halwa Puri is a beloved Pakistani breakfast, bringing together the delightful contrast of sweet, aromatic semolina halwa with light, fluffy, deep-fried puris. This iconic meal is often enjoyed on weekends or special occasions, offering a comforting and flavorful start to the day. Prepare to indulge in a truly authentic taste of Pakistan with this cherished dish.

ingredients.notes: optional, soaked in 1 tbsp warm water

instructions.title: Prepare the Puri Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour (if using), and salt. Add 2 tablespoons of oil and mix well until crumbly. Gradually add water, kneading until you form a soft, pliable, and smooth dough. The dough should be slightly firmer than chapati dough. Cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for at least 15-20 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare Halwa Syrup
instructions.text: In a saucepan, combine 2 cups of water, sugar, and crushed cardamom pods. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely. Reduce heat and let it simmer gently for 5 minutes. If using, add saffron strands and a pinch of orange food color to the syrup. Keep warm.

instructions.title: Cook the Semolina for Halwa
instructions.text: In a separate heavy-bottomed pan or wok, heat the ghee or butter over medium-low heat. Add the semolina and roast it, stirring continuously, until it turns light golden brown and releases a fragrant aroma. This usually takes about 8-10 minutes. Be careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Combine Halwa Ingredients
instructions.text: Carefully pour the hot sugar syrup into the roasted semolina, stirring vigorously to prevent lumps. The mixture will splutter, so be cautious. Continue stirring until all the liquid is absorbed and the halwa thickens, pulls away from the sides of the pan, and the ghee starts to separate. Cover the pan and let it cook on very low heat for 2-3 minutes to steam (dum).

instructions.title: Fry the Puris
instructions.text: While the halwa is on dum, heat a generous amount of oil in a deep frying pan or wok over medium-high heat for deep-frying the puris. Divide the rested puri dough into small, equal-sized balls. Roll each ball into a thin, round disc, about 4-5 inches in diameter. Carefully slide one puri into the hot oil. Gently press it down with a slotted spoon to make it puff up. Flip and fry until golden brown on both sides. Remove and drain excess oil on paper towels. Repeat for all puris.

instructions.title: Serve Halwa Puri
instructions.text: Garnish the hot halwa with sliced almonds and pistachios. Serve the warm, fluffy puris immediately alongside the sweet semolina halwa. For a complete Pakistani breakfast experience, you can also serve it with chickpea curry (chana masala) or potato curry (aloo tarkari).

tips: For extra soft puris, add a tablespoon of milk or yogurt to the dough while kneading. Ensure the dough is well-rested for maximum elasticity.
When frying puris, the oil must be very hot. If the oil isn't hot enough, the puris will absorb too much oil and become greasy instead of puffing up.
Halwa can be made a day in advance and stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Reheat gently before serving. Puris are best enjoyed fresh.
